story.headline: COP31 draft still omits fossil-fuel exit
story.summary: A new COP31 draft released on 22 November omits any explicit fossil-fuel exit; the EU and France rejected it as the summit overran by over 40 hours.
story.display_body: The COP31 presidency released a new draft final decision in Antalya early on Sunday 22 November that still names no exit from coal, oil or gas, and the EU and France rejected it as the summit ran more than 40 hours past its scheduled Friday close. The roughly ten-page text, prepared by the Turkish and Australian co-presidencies, refers only in passing to the 2023 Dubai decision (COP28) to "transition away" from fossil fuels. It acknowledges for the first time that warming will overshoot the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C goal, aiming to limit how far and for how long. It also calls for faster use of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS, technology that traps CO₂ from smokestacks, promoted by oil and gas companies) and a Turkish goal of raising electricity's share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035. French minister Monique Barbut called it "unacceptable" and said it "takes us backwards". Ireland's Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU presidency, said the chances of a deal were falling "by the hour", and an EU official told AFP there was a "very real possibility" of no agreement. COP president Murat Kurum said "the ball is now in the countries' court". Observers at the closed talks said Saudi Arabia and other oil producers pushed to keep fossil fuels out. The plenary to adopt the text was postponed repeatedly on Sunday morning, and many negotiators have already left, which raises the risk that too few are present to adopt it.
story.why: this was the clause Switzerland and about 30 other countries asked on Friday to have written into the final text. A decision that drops it, or no decision at all, would leave the 2023 Dubai wording as the high-water mark of UN climate diplomacy on fossil fuels.

story.headline: Drones set Russian freighter ablaze off Finland
story.summary: The US-sanctioned Russian cargo ship Sparta II was hit by drones Finland attributes to Ukraine and drifted burning into Finnish waters; a Russian helicopter allegedly violated Finnish airspace.
story.display_body: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after being hit by drones in the Gulf of Finland in the early hours of Saturday 21 November, and Finland's military said a Ukrainian attack was likely. The ship had left St Petersburg for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad on Friday evening. The Finnish military said it was damaged west of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 km off Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters; Russia's Leningrad region authorities said the strike was in international waters three nautical miles from the Russian border. Finnish Border Guard commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle the vessel has links to the Russian military and "it cannot be ruled out" that it carries military materiel. The ship is on a US sanctions list, and its crew evacuated into a life raft and rescue boat. A few hours later, at 12:34 local time, a Russian helicopter is suspected of entering up to 4.1 km into Finnish airspace off Loviisa, and Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said this may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations around the ship. Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote that "the war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas" and that Ukraine "has the right to fight against the aggressor". Finland has restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern part of the gulf and informed its NATO allies.
story.why: a burning Russian ship ended up in a NATO member's waters with a Russian aircraft following it in, so the war at sea has reached Finland's coast.

story.headline: Mexico captures cartel boss Chapo Isidro
story.summary: Mexican forces captured Beltrán Leyva leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa; 11 people including four soldiers were killed.
story.display_body: Mexican special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro", leader of the Beltrán Leyva organisation and one of the FBI's ten most-wanted fugitives, in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday 20 November; at least 11 people died in the fighting that followed. Mexico's Defence Ministry said the operation came out of intelligence coordination with US agencies. It said seven attackers and four soldiers on their way to reinforce Guasave were killed, and eight suspects were detained, among them his cousin and second-in-command Germán N ("Serafín") and his brother-in-law José N, the group's alleged financial operator. The three were flown to Mexico City early on Saturday and handed to organised-crime prosecutors. Meza Flores is wanted in Mexico for organised crime and drug offences and is subject to a US extradition order; the US had offered a $5 million reward. The ministry said it had "no report" of harm to uninvolved people, but Al Jazeera and AP describe videos of civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning vehicles and roadblocks, and military helicopters firing on locations across the city. US Ambassador Ronald Johnson praised the "sustained cooperation".
story.why: Meza Flores is allied with the "Mayos" faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which Washington lists as a terrorist organisation, and analysts warn that removing a boss can set off new fighting in a state already split between warring factions.

story.headline: Settler arson hits four West Bank villages
story.summary: Israel opened an investigation after settler arson in four West Bank villages; Gadi Eisenkot called it Jewish terrorism as he invited Likud to coalition talks.
story.display_body: Israeli authorities opened an investigation after vehicles and property were torched and vandalised overnight into Sunday 22 November in four West Bank villages, and Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form Israel's next government, called the attacks "Jewish terrorism". The army said soldiers and border police were sent to Deir As-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha'al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani after reports of burned cars and graffiti, and that it "strongly condemns" the acts. A Kafr Malik activist told AFP that settlers burned about eight vehicles there. Eisenkot, who came second in the late-October election and holds the mandate to form a government until the end of the month, called for the attackers to be arrested and severely punished. His Yashar party also invited Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud to "marathon" coalition talks starting Sunday. Likud's conditions include excluding Arab parties, rejecting a Palestinian state and keeping Israeli forces in occupied areas of Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, while Naftali Bennett, a key ally in Eisenkot's camp, said his party will not join Likud "under any circumstances". Since October 2023, at least 1,119 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank by soldiers or settlers, according to an AFP count based on Palestinian health ministry data, and at least 51 Israelis in Palestinian attacks or clashes, according to Israeli figures.
story.why: the man who could replace Netanyahu is condemning settler violence while negotiating with the party whose terms rule out a Palestinian state, so the coalition he builds will decide how much the condemnation counts for.

story.headline: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
story.summary: The EU and Indonesia signed a comprehensive economic partnership agreement and an investment protection agreement on 21 November.
story.display_body: The EU and Indonesia signed a free-trade agreement and an investment-protection agreement on Saturday 21 November, after almost ten years of negotiations. The Commission says the deal removes import duties on 98.5% of tariff lines for EU goods, saving EU exporters over €600 million a year, and projects EU exports to Indonesia to grow by almost 40% within 15 years. It also opens sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, pharmaceuticals and telecoms to EU investment and protects 221 EU geographical indications. Palm oil and deforestation were the main sticking points; the deal has a dedicated palm-oil protocol and makes the Paris climate agreement an "essential element". Ursula von der Leyen called it "one of the most ambitious deals" the EU has concluded in Asia. The European Parliament still has to give its consent, and the Commission expects provisional application in early 2027.
story.why: Swiss exporters already have their own route through the EFTA–Indonesia agreement, and EU firms are now set to reach Southeast Asia's largest economy on similar terms.

story.headline: Drone collapses Kyiv-region apartment block
story.summary: A Russian drone partly collapsed a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, Kyiv region; 14 people are missing.
story.display_body: A Russian drone struck a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, early on Sunday 22 November; part of it collapsed and 14 people are missing, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Nine people were evacuated and the fire was brought under control. Local authorities said two people were injured, among them a teenager, and rescuers are searching the rubble.

story.headline: Funeral boat capsizes in Nigeria
story.summary: An overcrowded boat carrying mourners capsized in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, killing at least 24.
story.display_body: At least 24 people died when an overcrowded boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in Bayelsa State, southern Nigeria, on Friday 20 November, the National Emergency Management Agency said. Police said the boat had a mechanical failure; residents told Reuters at least 300 people were on board. The pilot fled and the boat's manager was arrested.

story.headline: Journalists rally in Bern against cuts
story.summary: Hundreds of media workers rallied in Bern on 21 November against more than 360 Swiss media job cuts this year.
story.display_body: Several hundred journalists and media workers from all language regions rallied on Bern's Federal Square on Saturday 21 November under the slogan "Less journalism = less democracy", against a wave of newsroom cuts. The organisers, the Alliance des Médias, count more than 360 people laid off or whose jobs were cut in Swiss media this year, and say the real number is probably higher. This autumn Tamedia, Ringier and the public broadcaster SSR (including Swissinfo and RTS) have all announced restructurings, and titles such as Geneva's GHI and Lausanne Cités are closing. The alliance wants publishers and politicians to secure lasting funding for the sector. Caroline Gebhard, a journalist at La Côte and co-president of the union impressum, said the profession had come together "in record time" to sound the alarm.
story.why: Lausanne Cités is one of the closures, so this hits Vaud's local news directly.

story.headline: Pfister wants to keep defence department
story.summary: Defence minister Martin Pfister told NZZ he wants to keep the DDPS when departments are reassigned after the 9 December Federal Council election.
story.display_body: Defence Minister Martin Pfister said he wants to stay at the defence department (DDPS) when the Federal Council reassigns departments after the 9 December election to replace Guy Parmelin, in an NZZ interview published on Sunday 22 November. Pfister said the department is in a crisis of trust and that past failings, including at the arms company Ruag, must be "dealt with without mercy", with anything criminal or regulatory pursued "without ifs or buts". He said the systems the army wants to buy are "ready for procurement" and that what is missing is "the political decision to fund them".
